_about: Action and blood supply for muscles that already have a description and innervation, plus corrections where the innervation derived at build time is wrong. See app/extra_content.py.

Clavicular head of pectoralis major musc.action: Flexes the arm from the extended position, adducts and medially rotates the humerus.
Clavicular head of pectoralis major musc.blood_supply: Deltoid and pectoral branches of the thoraco-acromial artery.

Sternocostal head of pectoralis major mu.action: Adducts and medially rotates the humerus; extends the flexed arm against resistance; raises the ribs in forced inspiration when the arm is fixed.
Sternocostal head of pectoralis major mu.blood_supply: Pectoral branches of the thoraco-acromial artery, perforating branches of the internal thoracic artery and the lateral thoracic artery.

Abdominal part of pectoralis major muscl.action: Adducts and medially rotates the humerus and draws the shoulder downward.
Abdominal part of pectoralis major muscl.blood_supply: Pectoral branches of the thoraco-acromial and lateral thoracic arteries.

Subclavius muscle.action: Depresses and anchors the clavicle toward the sternum, protecting the subclavian vessels when the clavicle breaks.
Subclavius muscle.blood_supply: Clavicular branch of the thoraco-acromial artery.

Serratus anterior muscle.action: Protracts the scapula and holds it against the chest wall; its lower fibres rotate the glenoid upward for abduction above 90 degrees. Paralysis (long thoracic nerve injury) causes a winged scapula.
Serratus anterior muscle.blood_supply: Lateral thoracic, thoracodorsal and superior thoracic arteries.

Descending part of trapezius muscle.action: Elevates the scapula (shrugging) and rotates the glenoid upward; bilaterally extends the neck.
Descending part of trapezius muscle.blood_supply: Superficial branch of the transverse cervical artery and occipital artery.

Transverse part of trapezius muscle.blood_supply: Superficial branch of the transverse cervical artery.

Ascending part of trapezius muscle.action: Depresses the scapula and, with the upper fibres, rotates the glenoid upward.
Ascending part of trapezius muscle.blood_supply: Transverse cervical artery and dorsal branches of posterior intercostal arteries.

Levator scapulae.action: Elevates the scapula and rotates the glenoid downward; laterally flexes the neck.
Levator scapulae.blood_supply: Dorsal scapular and transverse cervical arteries.

Rhomboid major muscle.action: Retracts the scapula and rotates the glenoid downward; holds the scapula against the chest wall.
Rhomboid major muscle.blood_supply: Dorsal scapular artery and dorsal branches of posterior intercostal arteries.

Rhomboid minor muscle.action: Retracts the scapula and rotates the glenoid downward.

Clavicular part of deltoid muscle.action: Flexes and medially rotates the arm.
Clavicular part of deltoid muscle.blood_supply: Deltoid branch of the thoraco-acromial artery and anterior circumflex humeral artery.

Acromial part of deltoid muscle.action: Abducts the arm beyond the first 15 degrees initiated by supraspinatus.
Acromial part of deltoid muscle.blood_supply: Posterior circumflex humeral artery and acromial branch of the thoraco-acromial artery.

Scapular spinal part of deltoid muscle.action: Extends and laterally rotates the arm.

Supraspinatus muscle.action: Initiates abduction of the arm and holds the humeral head in the glenoid (rotator cuff). Its tendon is the one most often torn or impinged under the acromion.

Infraspinatus muscle.action: Laterally rotates the arm; stabilises the humeral head (rotator cuff).

Teres minor muscle.action: Laterally rotates the arm; stabilises the humeral head (rotator cuff).
Teres minor muscle.blood_supply: Circumflex scapular and posterior circumflex humeral arteries.

Coracobrachialis muscle.action: Flexes and adducts the arm; helps hold the humeral head in the glenoid.
Coracobrachialis muscle.blood_supply: Muscular branches of the brachial artery and anterior circumflex humeral artery.

Long head of biceps brachii.action: With the short head: supinates the forearm (powerfully when the elbow is flexed) and flexes the elbow; the long head also helps stabilise the humeral head.
Long head of biceps brachii.blood_supply: Muscular branches of the brachial artery and anterior circumflex humeral artery.

Short head of biceps brachii.action: With the long head: supinates the forearm and flexes the elbow; weakly flexes the shoulder.
Short head of biceps brachii.blood_supply: Muscular branches of the brachial artery.

Brachialis muscle.action: The main flexor of the elbow in every position of the forearm.
Brachialis muscle.blood_supply: Muscular branches of the brachial artery and radial recurrent artery.

Long head of triceps brachii.action: Extends the elbow; as it crosses the shoulder it also helps extend and adduct the arm.
Long head of triceps brachii.blood_supply: Profunda brachii and posterior circumflex humeral arteries.

Lateral head of triceps brachii.action: Extends the elbow, especially against resistance.

Medial head of triceps brachii.action: Extends the elbow; active in all extension, including unresisted.
Medial head of triceps brachii.blood_supply: Profunda brachii and superior ulnar collateral arteries.

Anconeus muscle.action: Assists triceps in elbow extension, tenses the joint capsule and abducts the ulna during pronation.
Anconeus muscle.blood_supply: Recurrent interosseous and middle collateral arteries.

Superficial head of pronator teres.action: Pronates the forearm and assists elbow flexion.
Superficial head of pronator teres.blood_supply: Ulnar and anterior ulnar recurrent arteries.

Deep head of pronator teres.action: Pronates the forearm. The median nerve passes between the two heads, where it can be compressed (pronator syndrome).

Flexor carpi radialis.action: Flexes and abducts (radially deviates) the wrist.

Palmaris longus muscle.action: Flexes the wrist and tenses the palmar aponeurosis. Absent in about 15% of people; its tendon is a common graft source.

Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.action: With the ulnar head: flexes and adducts (ulnar-deviates) the wrist.
Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.blood_supply: Ulnar artery and posterior ulnar recurrent artery.

Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.action: With the humeral head: flexes and adducts (ulnar-deviates) the wrist.
Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.blood_supply: Ulnar artery and posterior ulnar recurrent artery.

Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitorum su.action: Flexes the fingers at the proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints; assists wrist flexion.

Flexor digitorum profundus.action: The only muscle that flexes the distal interphalangeal joints of the fingers; also flexes the other finger joints and the wrist. Lateral half by the anterior interosseous (median) nerve, medial half by the ulnar nerve.

Flexor pollicis longus.action: Flexes the thumb, the only muscle flexing its interphalangeal joint.

Pronator quadratus.action: Prime pronator of the forearm; binds the radius and ulna together at the distal radio-ulnar joint.

Brachioradialis muscle.action: Flexes the elbow, most strongly with the forearm midway between pronation and supination.

Extensor carpi radialis longus.action: Extends and abducts (radially deviates) the wrist; stabilises the wrist during gripping.

Extensor carpi radialis brevis.action: Extends and abducts the wrist; its origin at the lateral epicondyle is the usual site of tennis elbow.

Abductor pollicis brevis.action: Abducts the thumb at the carpometacarpal and metacarpophalangeal joints. Wasting is an early sign of carpal tunnel syndrome.
Abductor pollicis brevis.blood_supply: Superficial palmar branch of the radial artery.

Superficial head of flexor pollicis brev.action: Flexes the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint.
Superficial head of flexor pollicis brev.blood_supply: Superficial palmar branch of the radial artery.

Deep head of flexor pollicis brevis.action: Flexes the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint.
Deep head of flexor pollicis brevis.blood_supply: Superficial palmar branch of the radial artery and deep palmar arch.

Opponens pollicis muscle.action: Opposes the thumb: flexes and medially rotates the first metacarpal so the thumb pad meets the fingertips.
Opponens pollicis muscle.blood_supply: Superficial palmar branch of the radial artery.

Oblique head of adductor pollicis.action: Adducts the thumb toward the palm, giving power to pinch grip. Weakness shows as Froment's sign.

Transverse head of adductor pollicis.action: Adducts the thumb toward the middle finger, giving power to pinch grip.

Abductor digiti minimi of hand.action: Abducts the little finger and helps flex its metacarpophalangeal joint.
Abductor digiti minimi of hand.blood_supply: Deep palmar branch of the ulnar artery.

Flexor digiti minimi of hand.action: Flexes the little finger at the metacarpophalangeal joint.
Flexor digiti minimi of hand.blood_supply: Deep palmar branch of the ulnar artery.

Opponens digiti minimi muscle of hand.action: Draws the fifth metacarpal forward and rotates it, deepening the palm and helping opposition with the thumb.
Opponens digiti minimi muscle of hand.blood_supply: Deep palmar branch of the ulnar artery.

Lumbrical muscles of hand.action: Flex the metacarpophalangeal joints and extend the interphalangeal joints of the fingers (the tabletop position).
Lumbrical muscles of hand.blood_supply: Superficial and deep palmar arches and digital arteries.

Dorsal interossei muscles of hand.action: Abduct the fingers from the axis of the middle finger (DAB); flex the metacarpophalangeal and extend the interphalangeal joints.

Palmar interossei muscles.action: Adduct the fingers toward the axis of the middle finger (PAD); flex the metacarpophalangeal and extend the interphalangeal joints.
Palmar interossei muscles.blood_supply: Palmar metacarpal arteries from the deep palmar arch.

Iliacus muscle.action: With psoas major (iliopsoas) flexes the hip and stabilises the hip joint; flexes the trunk on the fixed thigh.
Iliacus muscle.blood_supply: Iliac branch of the iliolumbar artery, deep circumflex iliac and obturator arteries.

Sartorius muscle.action: Flexes, abducts and laterally rotates the hip and flexes the knee (the cross-legged tailor's position).
Sartorius muscle.blood_supply: Muscular branches of the femoral artery.

Rectus femoris muscle.action: Extends the knee and flexes the hip (the kicking muscle).
Rectus femoris muscle.blood_supply: Descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery.

Vastus lateralis muscle.blood_supply: Descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery and perforating arteries.

Vastus medialis muscle.action: Extends the knee; its low oblique fibres (VMO) resist lateral displacement of the patella.
Vastus medialis muscle.blood_supply: Femoral artery and descending genicular artery.

Vastus intermedius muscle.blood_supply: Lateral circumflex femoral artery and profunda femoris.

Pectineus muscle.blood_supply: Medial circumflex femoral and obturator arteries.

Adductor longus.action: Adducts the hip and assists flexion and medial rotation. The commonest groin strain.

Adductor brevis.action: Adducts the hip and assists flexion.
Adductor brevis.blood_supply: Profunda femoris, medial circumflex femoral and obturator arteries.

Adductor magnus.action: Adductor part adducts and flexes the hip (obturator nerve); hamstring part extends the hip (tibial division of sciatic nerve).
Adductor magnus.blood_supply: Profunda femoris, perforating, obturator and femoral arteries.

Gracilis muscle.action: Adducts the hip, flexes the knee and medially rotates the flexed leg. Often used as a free muscle flap.
Gracilis muscle.blood_supply: Medial circumflex femoral artery (dominant) and profunda femoris.

Obturator internus.action: Laterally rotates the extended hip and abducts the flexed hip; holds the femoral head in the acetabulum.

Long head of biceps femoris.action: Extends the hip and flexes the knee; laterally rotates the flexed knee. Supplied by the tibial division of the sciatic nerve.
Long head of biceps femoris.blood_supply: Perforating arteries and inferior gluteal artery.

Short head of biceps femoris.action: Flexes the knee and laterally rotates the flexed leg. The only hamstring component supplied by the common fibular division.
Short head of biceps femoris.blood_supply: Perforating arteries and superior lateral genicular artery.

Semitendinosus muscle.action: Extends the hip, flexes the knee and medially rotates the flexed leg. Its tendon is a common ACL graft.
Semitendinosus muscle.blood_supply: Perforating arteries and inferior gluteal artery.

Semimembranosus muscle.action: Extends the hip, flexes the knee and medially rotates the flexed leg; its expansions reinforce the posterior knee capsule.

Tibialis anterior muscle.action: Dorsiflexes and inverts the foot; supports the medial arch. Weakness gives foot drop.

Extensor hallucis longus.action: Extends the great toe and dorsiflexes the ankle.

Extensor digitorum longus.action: Extends the lateral four toes and dorsiflexes and everts the foot.

Fibularis longus muscle.action: Everts and plantarflexes the foot; supports the transverse and lateral longitudinal arches.

Fibularis brevis muscle.action: Everts the foot and weakly plantarflexes it. Its pull can avulse the base of the fifth metatarsal in inversion injuries.

Medial head of gastrocnemius.action: With the lateral head and soleus (triceps surae): plantarflexes the ankle; flexes the knee.
Medial head of gastrocnemius.blood_supply: Sural branches of the popliteal artery.

Lateral head of gastrocnemius.action: With the medial head and soleus (triceps surae): plantarflexes the ankle; flexes the knee.
Lateral head of gastrocnemius.blood_supply: Sural branches of the popliteal artery.

Soleus muscle.action: Plantarflexes the ankle; its postural activity keeps the body from falling forward in standing, and its venous sinuses make it the calf muscle pump.
Soleus muscle.blood_supply: Posterior tibial, fibular and sural arteries.

Plantaris muscle.action: Weakly assists plantarflexion and knee flexion; its long tendon is used as a graft.
Plantaris muscle.blood_supply: Sural branches of the popliteal artery.

Calcaneal tendon.action: Transmits the pull of gastrocnemius, soleus and plantaris to the calcaneus, plantarflexing the ankle.
Calcaneal tendon.blood_supply: Posterior tibial and fibular arteries; its mid-portion 2-6 cm above the insertion is poorly vascularised and is where it usually ruptures.

Popliteus muscle.action: Unlocks the fully extended knee by laterally rotating the femur on the tibia (or medially rotating the tibia); pulls the lateral meniscus back.
Popliteus muscle.blood_supply: Inferior medial and lateral genicular arteries.

Tibialis posterior muscle.action: Inverts and plantarflexes the foot; the main dynamic support of the medial longitudinal arch. Its failure leads to adult-acquired flatfoot.

Flexor digitorum longus.action: Flexes the lateral four toes and plantarflexes the ankle; supports the longitudinal arch.

Flexor hallucis longus.action: Flexes the great toe (push-off in walking) and plantarflexes the ankle; supports the medial arch.

Extensor digitorum brevis.action: Assists in extending the second to fourth toes.
Extensor digitorum brevis.blood_supply: Lateral tarsal and dorsalis pedis arteries.

Extensor hallucis brevis.action: Extends the great toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint.

Abductor hallucis.action: Abducts and flexes the great toe; supports the medial arch.

Flexor digitorum brevis.action: Flexes the lateral four toes at the proximal interphalangeal joints; supports the longitudinal arch.

Abductor digiti minimi of foot.action: Abducts and flexes the little toe; supports the lateral arch.

Quadratus plantae muscle.action: Pulls on the tendon of flexor digitorum longus, straightening its line of pull and helping flex the toes.

Lumbrical muscles of foot.action: Flex the metatarsophalangeal joints and extend the interphalangeal joints of the lateral four toes. The first is supplied by the medial plantar nerve, the others by the lateral plantar nerve.
Lumbrical muscles of foot.blood_supply: Lateral plantar artery and plantar metatarsal arteries.

Medial head of flexor hallucis brevis.action: Flexes the great toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint; contains the medial sesamoid.
Medial head of flexor hallucis brevis.blood_supply: Medial plantar artery and first plantar metatarsal artery.

Lateral head of flexor hallucis brevis.action: Flexes the great toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint; contains the lateral sesamoid.
Lateral head of flexor hallucis brevis.blood_supply: Medial plantar artery and first plantar metatarsal artery.

Oblique head of adductor hallucis.action: Adducts the great toe and supports the transverse arch.
Oblique head of adductor hallucis.blood_supply: Plantar metatarsal arteries from the plantar arch.

Transverse head of adductor hallucis.action: Adducts the great toe and holds the metatarsal heads together, supporting the transverse arch.
Transverse head of adductor hallucis.blood_supply: Plantar metatarsal arteries from the plantar arch.

Flexor digiti minimi of foot.action: Flexes the little toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint.

Opponens digiti minimi muscle of foot.action: Draws the fifth metatarsal toward the sole (often fused with flexor digiti minimi).

Plantar interossei muscles.action: Adduct the third to fifth toes toward the second toe (PAD) and flex their metatarsophalangeal joints.

Dorsal interossei muscles of foot.action: Abduct the toes from the axis of the second toe (DAB) and flex the metatarsophalangeal joints.

Temporalis muscle.action: Elevates the mandible (closes the jaw); its posterior fibres retract it.
Temporalis muscle.blood_supply: Deep temporal branches of the maxillary artery and middle temporal branch of the superficial temporal artery.

Superficial part of masseter.action: Elevates the mandible for chewing; helps protrude it.
Superficial part of masseter.blood_supply: Masseteric branch of the maxillary artery, transverse facial and facial arteries.

Deep part of masseter.action: Elevates the mandible and helps retract it.
Deep part of masseter.blood_supply: Masseteric branch of the maxillary artery.

Medial pterygoid muscle.action: Elevates and protrudes the mandible; acting alone swings the jaw to the opposite side in grinding.
Medial pterygoid muscle.blood_supply: Pterygoid branches of the maxillary artery.

Superior head of lateral pterygoid muscl.action: Stabilises the articular disc and condyle of the temporomandibular joint during jaw closing.
Superior head of lateral pterygoid muscl.blood_supply: Pterygoid branches of the maxillary artery.

Inferior head of lateral pterygoid muscl.action: Pulls the condyle forward: protrudes the mandible and opens the mouth; unilaterally moves the jaw to the opposite side.
Inferior head of lateral pterygoid muscl.blood_supply: Pterygoid branches of the maxillary artery.

Anterior belly of digastric muscle.action: Depresses the mandible and raises the hyoid bone.
Anterior belly of digastric muscle.blood_supply: Submental branch of the facial artery.

Posterior belly of digastric muscle.action: Raises and retracts the hyoid bone; assists opening the mouth.

Mylohyoid muscle.action: Forms the floor of the mouth; raises the hyoid bone and floor of the mouth in swallowing; depresses the mandible.
Mylohyoid muscle.blood_supply: Mylohyoid branch of the inferior alveolar artery and submental artery.

Stylohyoid muscle.action: Raises and retracts the hyoid bone, elongating the floor of the mouth in swallowing.

Genioglossus muscle.action: Protrudes the tongue and depresses its centre; keeps the tongue from falling back and obstructing the airway. With a hypoglossal palsy the protruded tongue deviates to the weak side.
Genioglossus muscle.blood_supply: Sublingual and deep lingual branches of the lingual artery.

Hyoglossus muscle.blood_supply: Lingual artery (which runs deep to it).

Sternocleidomastoid muscle.action: Unilaterally tilts the head to the same side and turns the face to the opposite side; bilaterally flexes the neck and raises the sternum in forced inspiration.
Sternocleidomastoid muscle.blood_supply: Occipital and superior thyroid arteries (sternocleidomastoid branches) and suprascapular artery.

Bucinator.action: Presses the cheek against the teeth, keeping food between the molars and expelling air when blowing.

Orbicularis oris muscle.action: Closes and purses the lips; shapes them in speech.
Orbicularis oris muscle.blood_supply: Superior and inferior labial branches of the facial artery.

Orbital part of orbicularis oculi.action: Closes the eyelids tightly (screwing up the eyes) and wrinkles the surrounding skin.
Orbital part of orbicularis oculi.blood_supply: Facial, superficial temporal and ophthalmic artery branches.

Palpebral part of orbicularis oculi.action: Closes the eyelids gently in blinking and sleep; its lacrimal part helps drain tears. Facial palsy prevents eye closure, risking corneal exposure.
Palpebral part of orbicularis oculi.blood_supply: Palpebral branches of the ophthalmic artery.

Frontalis muscle.action: Raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead.
Frontalis muscle.blood_supply: Supra-orbital and supratrochlear arteries and frontal branch of the superficial temporal artery.

Occipitalis muscle.action: Pulls the scalp backward, anchoring the epicranial aponeurosis.

Temporoparietalis muscle.action: Tightens the scalp and raises the auricle.

Epicranial aponeurosis.action: Tendon sheet of occipitofrontalis, transmitting its pull across the scalp.

Corrugator supercilii.action: Draws the eyebrows down and medially, producing vertical frown lines.

Procerus muscle.action: Pulls the medial eyebrows down, producing transverse wrinkles over the bridge of the nose.

Nasalis muscle.action: Transverse part compresses the nasal aperture; alar part flares the nostrils.
Nasalis muscle.blood_supply: Superior labial and lateral nasal branches of the facial artery.

Depressor septi nasi.action: Pulls the nasal septum and tip downward.
Depressor septi nasi.blood_supply: Superior labial branch of the facial artery.

Levator nasolabialis.action: Levator labii superioris alaeque nasi: raises the upper lip and dilates the nostril (snarling).

Levator labii superioris.action: Raises and everts the upper lip.

Levator anguli oris.action: Raises the angle of the mouth.

Zygomaticus major muscle.action: Draws the angle of the mouth up and laterally in smiling.
Zygomaticus major muscle.blood_supply: Superior labial branch of the facial artery.

Zygomaticus minor muscle.action: Raises the upper lip, exposing the upper teeth.
Zygomaticus minor muscle.blood_supply: Superior labial branch of the facial artery.

Risorius muscle.action: Draws the angle of the mouth laterally (a grimace).
Risorius muscle.blood_supply: Superior labial branch of the facial artery.

Depressor anguli oris.action: Draws the angle of the mouth down and laterally (frowning).
Depressor anguli oris.blood_supply: Inferior labial branch of the facial artery.

Depressor labii inferioris.action: Pulls the lower lip down and laterally.
Depressor labii inferioris.blood_supply: Inferior labial branch of the facial artery and mental artery.

Mentalis muscle.action: Raises and protrudes the lower lip and wrinkles the skin of the chin (pouting).
Mentalis muscle.blood_supply: Inferior labial branch of the facial artery and mental artery.

Levator palpebrae superioris.action: Raises the upper eyelid; its smooth-muscle part (superior tarsal muscle) is sympathetic, so Horner syndrome gives a mild ptosis while third nerve palsy gives a complete one.
Levator palpebrae superioris.blood_supply: Muscular branches of the ophthalmic artery and supra-orbital artery.

Superior rectus muscle.action: Elevates the eye (best when abducted); also adducts and intorts it.
Superior rectus muscle.blood_supply: Muscular branches of the ophthalmic artery.

Inferior rectus muscle.action: Depresses the eye (best when abducted); also adducts and extorts it. Often entrapped in orbital floor blow-out fractures.
Inferior rectus muscle.blood_supply: Muscular branches of the ophthalmic artery and infra-orbital artery.

Medial rectus muscle.blood_supply: Muscular branches of the ophthalmic artery.

Inferior oblique muscle.action: Extorts the eye; elevates it, especially when adducted; weakly abducts.
Inferior oblique muscle.blood_supply: Muscular branches of the ophthalmic artery and infra-orbital artery.
